text.p: Algerian authorities have seized a weekly newspaper, the Islamist-leaning, Arabic-language Al Mouad, from the printing press in Algiers, the newspaper staff said on Thursday.
"We have learnt through the printing press (staff) that the newspaper was seized yesterday. But the authorities gave no reason for that," a newspaper staff member said by telephone from Algiers.
Abdelkader Talbi, a former television personality, is the director of Al Mouad.

The edition carried a commentary on the massacres of villagers and a story about late nationalist leader Emir Abdelkader whose residence in exile in Damascus, the newspaper said, had been transformed recently into a night club.
Abdelkader, seen in Algeria as the pioneer founder of the Algerian state, commands deep respect in Algeria.
Algeria's government, which is fighting a five-year-old conflict with Moslem guerrillas, wields huge power over the media.

Several newspapers and journals have been shut, usually for short periods, since 1993 when the army-backed authorities passed a law allowing them to ban newspapers carrying reports which they said threatened national security and public order.

The authorities impose tight censorship on security issues which has led Moslem rebels to accuse journalists of supporting the military-backed authorities, and make media staff the target of attacks. More than 60 media employees have been killed in the past 30 months.
Al Mouad has already been banned three times, including a six-month suspension period, in the past three years.
